headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI’s shared workspace state can conflict with MinerU’s MCP-enabled document pipeline, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the profiles’ mostly isolated I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can expose document content through an MCP server and API surfaces, while Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system that may ingest page content. No shared channel is documented, so the only clear bridge is manual or workspace-mediated content transfer, making hijack plausible but limited.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into a Notion page or Q&A prompt without review, injected instructions can be reinterpreted as guidance.
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize MinerU-produced text that contains adversarial instructions, the instructions may propagate.
mitigations: Paste only extracted facts, not raw MinerU output.
Strip imperative text before sending content to Notion AI.
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores embedded instructions.
Review any Notion-generated action items before acting on them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX, and Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases under the user’s Notion permissions. If MinerU outputs sensitive extracted text into Notion, that data flows into a vendor-hosted backend; the shared workspace path makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF MinerU output containing secrets is pasted into a Notion page, Notion AI may transmit that content to vendor backends.
IF the workspace contains regulated documents and Notion AI is used for Q&A on those pages, sensitive text can leave the local document-processing boundary.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in Notion pages used with AI.
Redact sensitive fields before importing MinerU output.
Restrict Notion AI use to non-sensitive workspaces.
Verify retention settings for the target workspace pages.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is concurrent and can use MCP, while Notion AI operates on shared workspace state across instances. Both can touch the same workspace-derived content, so overlapping writes or stale reads can occur even though neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem writes. Uncertainty about orchestration pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF MinerU-derived content is imported into a shared Notion page while another Notion AI session edits the same page, concurrent updates can overwrite or reorder content.
IF an MCP workflow writes structured outputs into a shared workspace, multiple instances may race on the same records.
mitigations: Assign one writer per page or database row.
Use page locks or a manual edit queue.
Separate staging pages from published pages.
Reconcile changes immediately after each import.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Notion AI can summarize or ground answers on. Notion AI’s RAG-style grounding means it may treat MinerU output as authoritative unless the operator verifies it, creating a default cascade from extraction errors into downstream knowledge work.
conditions: IF MinerU OCR misreads a table and the result is pasted into Notion, Notion AI may repeat the error in summaries or Q&A.
IF Notion AI is used to draft decisions from MinerU output without human verification, downstream actions can be based on false facts.
mitigations: Cross-check extracted numbers against the source document.
Require human review before publishing Notion summaries.
Keep source-document links alongside extracted claims.
Use a verification checklist for any decision-support output.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and uses downstream model providers under workspace permissions. If regulated or residency-bound content is moved from MinerU into Notion, the compliance posture changes materially; the profiles do not show a DPA or residency guarantee, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or other residency-bound data is imported from MinerU into Notion AI, it may be processed by vendor backends outside the original boundary.
IF the workspace contains regulated documents and Notion AI is enabled on those pages, retention and processor obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI-enabled pages.
Confirm residency and DPA terms before importing sensitive content.
Use a separate workspace for non-sensitive AI use.
Document retention and deletion procedures for imported content.
